correctness.rationale: The ambient metric bounds every skeleton route below by its sum of factor distances. For different moving coordinates, perform the initial coordinate's move to the target vertex first, the vertex-to-vertex moves next, and the move into the terminal interior last. For different underlying edges in the same moving coordinate, a factor shortest path must pass through a vertex, where all other moves can be inserted. On a single edge copy the direct subsegment is shortest: otherwise the factor edge's endpoints could be joined by a shorter route. For two distinct copies of the same geodesic edge of length ℓ, a route must project in the moving coordinate through a departure endpoint and an arrival endpoint. A common endpoint gives the horizontal lower bound s+t or 2ℓ−s−t (attainable while making all other moves there); opposite endpoints require at least ℓ in that projection, no better than the smaller common-endpoint cost. The other projections require their layer distance. Thus the detour is twice the minimum of the four distances of the two arclength positions from the endpoints. For z≥0 it exceeds z exactly when both coordinates are in (z/2,ℓ−z/2), with area (ℓ−z)_+². The b_i(b_i−1) ordered copy pairs, each of mass ℓ²/Λ², give the survival law; vertices are null. Integrating q z^{q−1} against the survival for q>0 yields the stated moment, and the scaled conditional survival is (1−z)² on [0,1]. The positive weights make the downward jumps of the one-sided second derivatives at all positive lengths identifiable. Finally, conditional on a distinct copy pair, at a threshold within x∈[0,ℓ] of the layer distance the ambient horizontal CDF is 2x/ℓ−(x/ℓ)² and the intrinsic horizontal CDF is (x/ℓ)² by two planar triangle area computations. Their difference is zero at the endpoints and elsewhere outside that interval; weighting recovers the exact correction and its strictness condition.

value.rationale: The one-skeleton restriction is a natural network-routing constraint. Detecting exactly when it matters transforms a potentially full edge-pair geometric problem into a shape-independent weighted spline; the correction retains layer-distance data and the derivative jumps recover the weighted aggregate length spectrum. For instance, two three-vertex path factors with edge lengths (1,1) and (2,2) have the same detour law and Λ as factors with (1,2) and (1,2); the theorem recovers the aggregate but cannot distinguish those allocations.
residual_risks: Does not infer topology or factor labels, cover nongeodesic edges, or compare ambient volume-uniform sampling.
